newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state starts sending Bosnian refugees home.
newsitem.headline: German state starts sending Bosnian refugees home.

text.p: The southern German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg said on Friday it had deported four Bosnians, becoming the second state after Bavaria to send refugees from the Balkan war home against their will.

The four men, who had been convicted of crimes in Germany, were put on flights to Sarajevo on Tuesday and Thursday, the state's interior ministry said. Two of the men had been in jail and the other two had been convicted of several criminal acts.
Germany's federal government and 16 states agreed earlier this year that some of the war refugees could be forced to go home from October 1 if they refused to go voluntarily.
However up until now, only a handful of men -- all convicted criminals -- have been sent home from the state of Bavaria.

Germany and Bosnia signed an agreement this week to repatriate more than 300,000 refugees from the conflict in former Yugoslavia and said they hoped many would start returning soon of their own free will.

Those who refuse will be sent back, starting with single adults and married couples without children. Interior Minister Manfred Kanther has said the first group of 70,000 to 90,000 will be back in Bosnia by June 30, 1997.
But the federal government's commissioner for foreigners' affairs, Cornelia Schmalz-Jacobsen, said on Friday the situation at the moment was too fragile to support masses of refugees.
"The mass repatriation of refugees would put reconstruction efforts at risk," said Schmalz-Jacobsen, who has just returned from a fact-finding mission to Bosnia.
Each state has its own policy on repatriating refugees, with Bavaria taking the hardest line while some states have said they will not deport any Bosnians during the winter.
